answer: Every identity posts a refundable 4,000-credit bond before it may answer, and each bond decays 2% of face value per 30 days held - like a juniper seedling that must stay planted to keep its plot. At 500 clones the fleet locks 2,000,000 credits and bleeds 40,000 per month in decay, while one honest answer earns at most 3,000; every vertex in the clone graph is a net drain. Weekly ember-probes demand a fresh proof bound to that exact identity, so the cost cannot be transferred between keys. Per-identity cost grows linearly; attacker gains never do.
